fields.name: signal_count
fields.doc:
`signalCount` — how many times this signal has FIRED.

A DIFFERENT wire field from `symbols_number`, and the two are easy to
confuse: native declares both on `OKTStgyInfoModel` — `symbolsNumber`
(`.h:535`, "Full currency pair count") and `signalCount` (`.h:593`,
"Signal trigger count"). Lifted here because the iOS Rust arm had no
field for it and was passing `symbols_number` in its place, so the share
card's "Signal trigger count" row rendered the pair count
(`OKTSOrderListUtil.m:1161-1162`). That row is the ONLY surface for this
value — the detail page itself never shows it, which is why the
substitution went unnoticed.

DECLARED LAST, and that position is load-bearing. Field order IS the
FFI contract: the generated Kotlin constructor is positional, so a
defaulted field only spares an existing call site if every
non-defaulted field still sits at the index that site passes. This
field first landed between `symbols_number` and `win_rate`, which left
`max_drawdown` unfilled for every Kotlin site passing the pre-MR
argument list — and adding the default there would NOT have fixed that,
because the shifted list still runs one argument short. Appending after
the whole defaulted block is what actually keeps those sites compiling.
Do not sort this back up next to `symbols_number` for readability.

name: place_order_from_state
doc:
Submit the order using the basket Rust already owns.

Prefer this over [`Self::place_order_with_coins`], which takes the
coin list as an argument. Refuses a basket that
`is_coin_allocation_valid` rejects, so a native call site that
missed a disabled Confirm cannot post ratios the server will bounce.
Submit the order Rust already holds. Returns whether it was ACCEPTED.

`false` means it was refused locally and no effect was spawned, so no
result and no error will follow — the caller must undo whatever it did in
anticipation (native shows a loading HUD before calling, and that HUD is
dismissed by the result/error sinks, so a silent refusal would leave it
spinning forever). This return value is the whole reason the refusal is
safe to have: native has its own inline allocation error and normally
blocks first, but the two checks read different copies of the basket —
native reads the ObjC mirror, which is a MainActor hop behind and can be
a strict SUBSET of Rust's (`mirrorRustBasketIntoItem` skips a ccy it
cannot resolve and bails on an empty result) — so they can disagree.

name: format_grid_profit_text
doc:
G7 — grid profit-text COMPOSITE. Returns the PARTS (not the assembled string).

Replicates legacy `buildGridProfitText` (StrategyConvert.kt:421-491), whose
amounts route through `getBotPnl(isShowUnit = false, isShowSymbol = false)` →
`getBotPrecision` and whose blank-decision routes through `getDigitPnl`. The
two legacy precisions are NOT the same and must be modeled separately:

* **Displayed amount** (`getBotPnl` → `getBotPrecision`,
StrategyConvert.kt:279-305): precision = `max(pairDigit, currencyDigit)`
where `pairDigit = getPnlPrecision(instId, instType)` = the SPOT
`createProfitConverterWithIndex` `quote_dig` (`resolve_profit_digit`,
fallback 0) and `currencyDigit = getTradeCoinInfo(unit)?.sizeDig`
(`resolve_get_bot_precision_coin_digit`, **fallback 0 — no 4**). Per-sign
DOWN(>0)/UP(≤0), drop zeros, AUTO sign, no `+`, no color.
* **Blank decision** (`getDigitPnl`, StrategyConvert.kt:373-398):
`digit = max(currencyDigit, pairDigit)`, then `if digit == 0 →
RECURRING_DEFAULT_DIGIT(4)`, per-sign rounding; `isAmtBlank` is
`getDigitPnl(min).eq("0") || getDigitPnl(max).eq("0")`. The `4` floor here
only bites when BOTH `quote_dig` and the coin `sizeDig` are absent.

`unit` is the legacy `getPnlUnit(instId, instType, profit_ccy)`; for the SPOT
create flow that resolves to `profit_ccy` (the quote ccy) — passed through
directly. `inst_type` is part of the legacy signature, kept for a 1:1 native
call shape; the SPOT digit sources key on the inst id / ccy (SPOT inst family
== inst id).

to select them, and the seeding pass skips them.

Derived from the instrument's `bizStatus`, NOT from native's separate
countdown store. That is a deliberate, documented difference: core-trading
treats `bizStatus` as the authoritative gate (its own
`new_coin_count_down_use_case` says so, with the countdown model as
optional detail), and the store native reads
(`OKTrade.instCountDownDataManager`) is not reachable from Rust. Residual
skew: the two are fed by different channels, so around the instant a coin
goes live one may flip before the other.

fields.name: registry_name
fields.doc:
The coin REGISTRY's display name, e.g. `bitcoin`.

Not a duplicate of [`Self::coin_full_name`], and the two must not be
substituted for one another. That one is the INSTRUMENT's `coinName`; this is
`TradeCoinInfo.name` out of `public/coins`. Native read them at different call
sites from different objects — the search list from the instrument, the picker
sheet from `coinsBySymbol[symbol].name` — so both are carried rather than one
being assumed to stand in for the other. They may well hold the same text;
that is not the same as being the same field.

Empty when the registry has no entry for this coin.

fields.name: groups

empty when the registry has no entry — the picker's own `?? []` covered both.

fields.name: list_time

fields.name: icon_url

Empty is a real, expected outcome rather than an error, and the caller
MUST handle it: native's `imageURLForCoin:` synthesizes a CDN url from
`OKFResourceAcceleratorManager` when the registry misses, which is exactly
the case for a coin that is listed but absent from `public/coins` — i.e.
the [`Self::is_waiting_online`] rows. That synthesis needs platform
configuration Rust has no access to, so it stays native. The split is
deliberate: the DATA (registry url) comes from here, the PLATFORM CONFIG
(CDN domain) stays where it is owned, and neither needs `OKTrade`.

name: seed_info_from_entry
doc:
Seed `info` from the bot-list ENTRY payload, before the detail fetch
lands, so the Overview card renders at its real height on first frame
instead of growing from zero when the first HTTP push arrives.

`json` is the raw wire row the bot list already holds for this bot
(`OKTSHoardCoinOrderModel`). It is parsed with the SAME
`SmartPortfolioStrategyInfoResponse` DTO and run through the SAME
`into_domain()` as the HTTP response, so the display twins come out of
one formatter and the seed cannot drift from the fetched render. That
single-funnel property is the whole reason the seed crosses into Rust
rather than being formatted natively.

Deliberately narrow — it writes `info` and NOTHING else:

1. **`info_json` stays `None`.** That field is the WS merge base, and
`apply_ws_update` drops a partial frame when there is no base (see the
invariant on that fn). The entry row carries FEWER fields than the
detail payload, so promoting it to the merge base would let a delta
merge onto an incomplete base — the defect that invariant exists to
prevent.
2. **`info_state` is untouched.** The screen gates success / no-data /
error rendering on it; a seed is not a fetch result.
3. **An existing `info` is never overwritten.** Fetched data must not be
downgraded to a seed, and a second seed call is a no-op.
4. **An unusable payload changes no state** — never blank what is there.
That covers both a hard parse failure AND a payload that deserializes
without being an entry row: every DTO field is `#[serde(default)]` and
`serde` accepts a sequence for a struct, so `"[]"` / `"{}"` would
otherwise seed an all-empty record whose twins are every
`Placeholder` — a fully-populated `--` header. A non-empty `algoId` is
the entry-row test.

`order_status` is left alone too: it is driven by the fetch / WS paths.

name: resync_coins_for_quote_ccy
doc:
Re-align the basket with a new quote currency.

Drops assets that are not tradable in `quote_ccy`, then seeds one if the basket is
empty afterwards — which includes having been empty on entry. Survivors keep their price
bounds, and their ratios follow native `OKTRecurringItem.removeSelectedCoin:`
exactly: an EVEN basket is re-split over the survivors, an uneven one keeps its
ratios and leaves the deficit visible rather than silently reshaping the user's
split.

This doc used to say the ratios were never rebalanced, "same rule as
`remove_coin`" — wrong twice over, since that method DID rebalance an even basket
and so does native. `remove_coin` itself is gone now; `retain_coins_in_universe`
is the only implementation of the rule.

`fallback_universe` is the eligible base currencies NATIVE computed for
`quote_ccy`, used only when this crate's own read comes back empty. That read is
`bot_recurring_seed_universe`, which opens with `if !ct_enabled { return
Vec::new() }` — so for the core-trading control cohort it is ALWAYS empty and this
method could never prune anything. Rust's basket then kept assets that are not
tradable in the new currency, permanently: `set_coins` has no universe gate, so a
picker selection lands whatever it is given and nothing can ever remove it again.
Native has the universe on either cohort (it walks OKTrade's instrument store), so
it hands it over rather than the alternative — reconciling two baskets in Swift,
which took three attempts and broke something each time.

Pass it EMPTY to keep the old behaviour: no prune, and no reseed, when this crate
cannot see the instruments.

The trailing reseed uses the SAME resolved universe — it must, or a prune from the
fallback could empty a basket the reseed then cannot refill. Callers therefore need
to hand over a list that means "listed AND tradable", matching what this crate's own
read returns; native filters its not-yet-live instruments before passing it.
`seed_default_coin` is unaffected and still reads only this crate's own universe.

name: recurring_coin_info_warmed
doc:
[`recurring_coin_info`], but it WAITS for the coin registry first.

For callers that are not preceded by a warm-up. The synchronous read answers
`None` on a cold store and does not prime it, which is safe on the place-order
page — its `performNativeSetup` awaits `recurring_search_universe`, so the
store is warm by the time anything reads it — and was NOT safe on the
order-detail action sheets. Reached from the running-bots list nothing primes this
store — a strategy detail does, but only on the Rust cohort — so `coinId` came back nil and
the Edit-amount / Invest-more sheets refused to build at all: a dead button
with no feedback. That shipped (iOS `fb646c0b4`).

## What the await buys, and what it does NOT

It removes the ORDERING race: this caller no longer reads before the load
that primes the store. It does NOT promise the store is populated
afterwards. `ensure_trade_data_loaded` returns `()` and swallows every error
it meets — four sites in `trade_data_preload.rs`, by design, because "a load
failure must NOT abort the bot-info fetch". Offline, a `/coins` 5xx, or a
`NoDataFound` all leave the registry cold and this function still answers
`None`.

So `None` means "unknown coin OR the warm-up could not complete". A caller
must degrade the one value that needed it and must NOT tell the user (or a
log reader) that the currency does not exist — it cannot know that.

## Cost: treat it as a network call

Not a completed future on the first call. `ensure_coins_loaded` keys off a
login-state marker initialised to `-1`, so the first call in a process always
takes the forced branch and awaits a `/coins` round trip, and `load_spot_biz`
can add `/simpleProduct` + `/config`. By this function's own premise its
callers ARE that first caller, so give it a loading state.

## Why a second export rather than reusing the exported warm-up

iOS awaiting the already-exported `ensure_bot_trade_data_loaded` and then
calling the synchronous read would need no new export — but that one is gated
on `use_core_trading_rust()`, so it would no-op for the control cohort and
leave the dead button live there. This awaits the UNGATED
`ensure_trade_data_loaded` instead, so both cohorts warm. The gate difference
is deliberate: do not "restore" it by following that precedent, which is a
precedent for the cancellation SHAPE only.

A cancelled call yields `None`. Neither shipped iOS caller retains the token
it constructs, so neither can currently cancel.
